plan: Sell SOXL and SPAL to zero to eliminate leveraged ETF exposure.

conservative.read: This conservative plan targets around 1.5% per month, focusing on capital preservation. It significantly reduces risk by cutting leveraged ETFs and lowering concentration, aiming for steady, low-drawdown performance.

moves.note: Add quality tech, strong scanner setup

plan: Trim SOXL to 3% and SPAL to 1% to reduce leveraged ETF exposure.
Trim SPY to 25% to reduce concentration and meet the mandate.
Buy RTX, targeting 4%, as a new quality tech addition from scanner setups.
Trim CRWD to 10% to reduce single name concentration.
This plan balances risk and growth, maintaining a small leveraged ETF presence.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets around 2.5% per month, prioritizing risk-first growth. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while blending broad index exposure with quality tech, aiming for moderate growth with controlled risk.

plan: Add to SOXL and SPAL, targeting 6% each, to increase leveraged ETF exposure.
Buy RTX, targeting 6%, and CVX, targeting 4%, from top scanner setups.
Add to CRWD, maintaining 14%, to concentrate in a working name.
Trim SPY to 25% to meet the concentration mandate.
This plan stretches for growth, using leverage and concentrating in strong setups.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets around 4% per month, aiming for stretch growth. It significantly increases exposure to leveraged ETFs and concentrates in high-scoring setups. Be aware this raises both upside and drawdown potential, and leveraged ETFs decay daily, meaning substantial losses can occur quickly without strict stop discipline.

plan: Sell SOXL and SPAL to zero to eliminate all leveraged ETF exposure.
Add to QQQI, targeting 30%, to rotate into income-focused ETFs.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and favor income.
Sell CRWD and SMH to zero to exit high-beta single names.
This plan prioritizes steady monthly distributions and low drawdown.
income.read: This income plan targets around 1% per month, focusing on parking cash for yield. It rotates heavily into income/covered-call ETFs and broad index, cutting leverage and high-beta names. While prioritizing low drawdown and reliable income, distributions are variable and NAV can still fall in a selloff.
